segments.en: Therefore Avraham purchased Me'aras HaMachpailah from Efron. Efron is the aspect of afar [earth/dust] — the evil that grips the element of earth: "V'nachash afar lachmo" — "The serpent's food is dust" (Yeshayah 65:25); "V'afar tochal" (Bereishis 3:14). This is the aspect of atzvus [melancholy], atzlus [laziness], and heaviness — drawn from the evil within the element of earth, which is the essential bite of the serpent, as our Rebbe said regarding this verse (LM II:189). 1

This is the aspect of the tisurah [base/platform] of the Tefillin, whose meaning is a bridge. From it emerges the ma'abarta [passage]. This is the essential part that rests upon the body — for from the Tefillin, only the tisurah and the ma'abarta touch the skin of the head and arm. This is the essential thing we must receive from the holy Tefillin: to draw from them a bridge to cross this world in peace — to pass over all obstacles and confusions and draw truly close to Hashem. 4

segments.he: ענין תפילין על פי המאמר המתחיל ואתם תהיו לי ממלכת כהנים וכו' המדבר מהעלאת היראה (סימן ט"ו) המתחיל מי שרוצה לטעום טעם אור הגנוז הוא צריך להעלות היראה לשרשה דהיינו לדעת, ובמה מעלין על ידי משפט שישפוט את עצמו וכו' וכשזוכין לדעת זוכין לבחינת תורה שבנגלה זוכין לפלה שהיא בחינת חסד לאברהם, ועל ידי תפלה במסירת נפש זוכין לתורה שבנסתר שהוא אור הגנוז משבעת ימי בראשית עיין שם כל זה היטב:
segments.en: This is the aspect of the three wrappings on the middle finger, which is on the level of Yaakov and Moshe — the bariach hatichon [middle bolt] running through the beams from end to end (as explained in the Yanuka, Parshas Balak). Therefore the binding of the Tefillin's strap concludes there — for then emunah is completed in perfection through Tefillin. 11

segments.he: וכל זה הוא בחינת תפילין כי עיקר התפילין הוא להעלות היראה לשרשה כי תפילין הם בחינת יראה כידוע כמו שאמרו רז"ל (מנחות לה) וראו כל עמי הארץ כי שם ה' נקרא עליך ויראו ממך אלו תפילין וכו' גם תפילין הם בחינת מוחין ודעת היינו להעלות היראה לשרשה שבדעת וזה בחינת תפילין של יד ותפילין של ראש כי תפילה של יד היא בחינת יראה בחינת יד כהה, ותפילין שבראש היא בחינת שורש היראה שבדעת בחינת ראש ומוחין והדעת הנ"ל הוא בחינת תורה כנ"ל וזה בחינת הפרשיות של תפילין שהם תורה וזה בחינת קריאת שמע שאומרים בתפילין שהוא תורה, ועל ידי זה זוכין לתפלה וזהו שמתפללין בתפילין, ועל ידי זה זוכין לאור הגנוז זה בחינת אורות המקיפין שנתגלין על ידי התפילין שהם בחינת תורה שבנסתר בחינת אור הגנוז, וזה בחינת שין של ג' ראשין שין של ד' ראשין זה בחינת אור הגנוז שהיא אור שבעת הימים בחינת ז' ראשין הנ"ל:
segments.en: This is the aspect of the knot shaped like a Yud at the shel Yad — the aspect of supporting the fallen. They receive their moaach and chiyus — to revive themselves and not fall completely — through Tefillin shel Yad, as explained above. The Yud-knot = the illumination of tzadik Yesod Olam to Malchus (= Kneses Yisrael). Therefore one must be very careful that this knot sits close to the shel Yad — for the essential illumination of Mochin for the common people (revived by the Shechinah from their fall) comes through the tzadik Yesod Olam whose perception is so exalted that he can revive and support all the fallen. 14

segments.he: כי רוב המאמרים של רבינו ז"ל שנאמרו ב~ אותן הזמנים כולם נאמרו על תפילין כך נשמע מפיו הקדוש בפירוש ואף על פי שכל מאמר כלול מכל התורה כולה אף על פי כן ביחוד היתה כוונתו בכמה וכמה מאמרים שנאמרו אז על מצות תפילין:
segments.en: This is the aspect of the yahrzeit — when one fasts on the day of a parent's death, recites Kaddish, and lights a candle. All this is to elevate the neshamah of the deceased to the arichas chayim (= eternal life that the tzadikim merit in the World to Come). This is done each year on the day of death — for the day of death is the true beginning of one's life, each person according to what he merited through his holy service, since this world is a passing shadow and its life is not truly life at all. The essential arichas chayim = renewing one's chiyus at all times, especially each year (= Rosh HaShanah). Therefore one works for the tikun of the departed each year on his death-day (= the beginning of his chiyus = his personal Rosh HaShanah). 24

segments.he: ועיקר אור התפילין זוכין על ידי קימת חצות ועוסקין בתורה, ועל ידי זה חוט של חסד נמשך ביום (חגיגה יב) ועל ידי זה זוכין לתפילין כמובן בכוונות, קימת חצות זה בחינת העלאת היראה לשרשה על ידי בחינת משפט כי קודם חצות אומרים ווידוי על החטאים זה בחינת משפט ששופט את עצמו על כל מה שעשה, ואחר כך מתאבלין על חורבן בית המקדש שזהו בחינת תיקון המשפט כי חורבן בית המקדש הוא פגם המשפט כי מקום המשפט היה בבית המקדש וכשנחרב נאמר (קהלת ג) מקום המשפט שמה הרשע כמו שאמרו רז"ל (ויקרא רבא פרק ד'), כי בית המקדש היה כלול מכל הבחינות הנ"ל כי שם מקום היראה בחינת ירושלים יראה שלם (בראשית רבה פרק נ'), וגם הוא בחינת דעת כמו שאמרור ז"ל (ברכות לג) היינו העלאת היראה לדעת על ידי המשפט שהיה שם בבית המקדש בלשכת הגזית שהיו יושבין שם בית דין הגדול לעשות משפט למטה לבטל הדין של מעלה ושם מקום התורה כמו שכתוב (דברים יז) על פי התורה אשר יורוך:
segments.en: The entirety of this discourse revolves around the foundation built upon the story of the first Beggar of the Seven Beggars — the Blind one — who gave the couple a gift as a d'rashah: long life. As our Rebbe himself explained with his holy mouth, after telling the story of the second day (about the Deaf Beggar) — he said afterward: "The first one gave them arichas chayim, and this..." For the essential aspect of Tefillin is to merit arichas chayim — to begin living anew each time, true life in Avodas Hashem, as explained above at length. 28

aligned_segments.en: The parchment of Tefillin must be from the hide of a kosher domesticated animal, wild animal, or bird, as it says: "L'ma'an…" — from a species that is permitted to your mouth, etc.

aligned_segments.he: ענין תפילין על פי המאמר המתחיל ואתם תהיו לי ממלכת כהנים וכו' המדבר מהעלאת היראה (סימן ט"ו) המתחיל מי שרוצה לטעום טעם אור הגנוז הוא צריך להעלות היראה לשרשה דהיינו לדעת, ובמה מעלין על ידי משפט שישפוט את עצמו וכו' וכשזוכין לדעת זוכין לבחינת תורה שבנגלה זוכין לפלה שהיא בחינת חסד לאברהם, ועל ידי תפלה במסירת נפש זוכין לתורה שבנסתר שהוא אור הגנוז משבעת ימי בראשית עיין שם כל זה היטב:
aligned_segments.en: According to the Torahs "Hai man d'azeil l'minsav ittesa" (Siman 29) and "Tefillah LaChavakuk" (Siman 19), see there. Tefillin are the rectification of Da'as, for they are the aspect of Mochin [brains/intellect]. And they are the aspect of the Tikkun HaKlali [General Rectification] — the rectification of the Bris, for the rectification of Da'as is the rectification of the Bris. Therefore, the essential content of Tefillin is the remembrance of Yetzias Mitzrayim, for the Exodus is the aspect of rectifying the Bris and Da'as. In Mitzrayim there was the blemish of the Bris and Da'as, as explained many times. Therefore it says of the exile in Mitzrayim: "Va'e'evor alayich… v'at eirom v'eryah" — "And I passed over you… and you were naked and bare" (Yechezkel 16:6–7) — for they were naked, without garments, because the Tikkun HaKlali, which is the rectification of garments, had not yet been achieved. And it says there nearby: "Va'e'evor alayich va'er'eich misboseses bedamayich" — "And I passed over you and saw you wallowing in your blood" — for one depends on the other. She was naked and bare because she was wallowing in blood — the aspect of dam niddah [menstrual blood], the aspect of "Adom lilbushecha" — "Red is Your garment" — which is the corruption of garments. When Hashem wished to rectify and redeem them, it says: "Va'omar lach bedamayich chayi" — "And I said to you: In your blood, live!" — the aspect of: the blood becomes turbid and turns to milk (Niddah 9a), which is the aspect of life — the infant's sustenance — "V'dei chalev izim l'lachmecha… v'chayim l'na'aroseicha" (Mishlei 27:27). The blood is whitened through elevating the Mochin. The Mochin are life itself: "HaChochmah techayeh" — "Wisdom gives life" (Koheles 7:12) — the opposite of the corruption of garments through stains, the aspect of dam niddah, which is the side of death. As our Sages said (Shabbos 114a): "A talmid chacham on whose garment a stain is found is deserving of death" — for stains come from the 365 sinews corresponding to the 365 negative commandments, whence the side of death derives. Therefore it says there immediately after "bedamayich chayi": "Va'albisheich va'en'aleich" — "And I clothed you and shod you" — for through the blood becoming turbid and turning to milk, the garments are rectified. Therefore on the night of the Exodus one drinks four cups of wine — in the aspect of: "merited — he becomes a head" (Yoma 76b), as explained there (Siman 29). They correspond to the four white garments that the Kohen Gadol wears on Yom HaKippurim, when the blood becomes turbid and turns to milk — the aspect of the scarlet thread that whitens sins. The four white garments indicate that the Mochin — which are four: Chochmah, Binah, and Da'as which divides into two (Chassadim and Gevuros) — have been rectified. Then from Da'as comes speech, which contains Chassadim and Gevuros, fire and water. As written there: through the Tikkun HaKlali (rectification of Da'as), one can speak. Corresponding to this are the four parshiyos of Tefillin — corresponding to the four white garments — for Tefillin are the Tikkun HaKlali. This is the aspect of the Shin of three heads and Shin of four heads. When Yisrael left Mitzrayim — from the blemish of the Bris — they needed to count seven weeks corresponding to the seven clean days of a niddah, for they emerged from the aspect of dam niddah. They are seven corresponding to the seven orifices of the brain, which are the aspect of the seven lamps of the Menorah that must be rectified when the Mochin are elevated. Corresponding to this are the seven days of mourning (rachamana litzlan), to draw down the Mochin that departed at death — for the essential death is the departure of the Mochin, since "HaChochmah techayeh." This is the aspect of the seven days the one contaminated by a corpse must count. And this is the aspect of the seven heads of the two Shins (three plus four) — corresponding to the seven clean days, to rectify the Mochin. They are divided into three and four because the Mochin are so divided: initially, before entering within, they are three; afterward, when they enter, Da'as divides into two and they become four. Thus the seven days of mourning are also divided into three and four, for the first three days have stricter laws (Yoreh De'ah 393:1). Similarly, the seven days of a corpse require sprinkling on the third and seventh. And the seven clean days of a niddah — the first three are stricter regarding a stain (ibid. 196:10). For the Mochin too are divided: in the first three days the Mochin have not yet begun to be rectified at all; afterward they have already been drawn down in those three days and are close to entering — hence afterward it is not as strict. From all the above, Tefillin are the aspect of the Tikkun HaKlali — rectification of the Bris. The essential rectification of the Bris is through the completeness of Leshon HaKodesh [the Holy Tongue], as our Rebbe said (Siman 19). Through Tefillin, speech of Leshon HaKodesh is rectified, as Rashi explains: "V'hayu l'totafos" — its Targum is "viy'hon l'shinunin" — that whoever sees them speaks of the miracle. Thus through Tefillin, speech of praise and thanks to Hashem is rectified — the completeness of Leshon HaKodesh. Therefore the essential Tefillin are made of hide — the parchment is of hide, the batim [housings] are of hide, and if made of gold they are invalid. For the completeness of Leshon HaKodesh comes through Leshon Targum [the Aramaic tongue] — by elevating the good within the Targum. This is the aspect of hide, for hide is the aspect of Nogah [the intermediate shell] — a mixture of good and evil, which is the aspect of Targum (also the aspect of Nogah). Therefore Tefillin must be written on hide and constructed from hide — to elevate the good from Nogah into Leshon HaKodesh, to fulfill "V'hayu l'totafos" and its Targum "viy'hon l'shinunin." They must be from a permitted species specifically, for the permitted species is the aspect of Targum/Nogah from which the good is elevated to Leshon HaKodesh. But the forbidden species are the aspect of the evil of the 70 languages that must be subdued, as explained there — "Yimotu aleihem gechalim" — "Let coals fall upon them."

aligned_segments.he: וכל זה הוא בחינת תפילין כי עיקר התפילין הוא להעלות היראה לשרשה כי תפילין הם בחינת יראה כידוע כמו שאמרו רז"ל (מנחות לה) וראו כל עמי הארץ כי שם ה' נקרא עליך ויראו ממך אלו תפילין וכו' גם תפילין הם בחינת מוחין ודעת היינו להעלות היראה לשרשה שבדעת וזה בחינת תפילין של יד ותפילין של ראש כי תפילה של יד היא בחינת יראה בחינת יד כהה, ותפילין שבראש היא בחינת שורש היראה שבדעת בחינת ראש ומוחין והדעת הנ"ל הוא בחינת תורה כנ"ל וזה בחינת הפרשיות של תפילין שהם תורה וזה בחינת קריאת שמע שאומרים בתפילין שהוא תורה, ועל ידי זה זוכין לתפלה וזהו שמתפללין בתפילין, ועל ידי זה זוכין לאור הגנוז זה בחינת אורות המקיפין שנתגלין על ידי התפילין שהם בחינת תורה שבנסתר בחינת אור הגנוז, וזה בחינת שין של ג' ראשין שין של ד' ראשין זה בחינת אור הגנוז שהיא אור שבעת הימים בחינת ז' ראשין הנ"ל:
aligned_segments.en: This is why our Sages were precise in deriving the law that Tefillin must be from "a species permitted to your mouth" — "hamutar l'ficha" specifically. This is the aspect of holy eating — elevating and illuminating the letters within the food through eating, which is the completeness of Leshon HaKodesh, as explained in the Torah "Tefillah LaChavakuk." Therefore the Torah forbids eating forbidden things — for they are the aspect of the evil of the 70 languages, where the letters cannot illuminate and sparkle. Only the permitted things, the aspect of Targum, are rectified and their letters illuminate through eating — elevating the good within them. Therefore Tefillin too must be from a permitted species. And see in "Tefillah LaChavakuk" regarding the completeness of Leshon HaKodesh through Leshon Targum, where it is explained that through meriting the completeness of Leshon HaKodesh, one merits that his eating and pleasures come only from the sparkling of the letters within the food — the essential rectification of eating in holiness. The mitzvah of Tefillin according to the teaching "V'atem tih'yu li mamleches Kohanim v'goy kadosh" (Siman 34), see there the entire teaching. The essential principle: through the holy Nekudah [point] — the light of holy love that dwells in the aspect of Tzaddik/Yesod, which is revealed and illuminates through the mouth, "Pi yedaber Chochmos" — "My mouth shall speak wisdoms" — through this it illuminates to the fallen loves that come from the shattering of the vessels of Chesed, which fell into the heart and break the heart. Through the light of this Nekudah, they become bound and return to holiness, and all the fallen loves are nullified. This Nekudah must be received in three aspects (minei ubei): by speaking between oneself and one's Creator; by receiving from one's fellow — "umkablin dein min dein" — for each Jew has a good point that his fellow does not, making him a Tzaddik relative to his fellow, and one must receive from that point; and all these points must receive from the comprehensive Nekudah that resides with the Tzaddik HaDor, the root-soul of Yisrael. The Nekudah is in the aspect of Melupum [cholam vowel], the aspect of Yesod — "Harchev picha va'amal'eihu" — "Open your mouth wide and I shall fill it." It is in multiple aspects that are Yud-Vav — the Tzaddik and the totality of Yisrael, and also "Pi yedaber" and "Hagos libi tevunos" — "My heart's meditation is understanding" — also Yud-Vav, and likewise the totality of Torah, see there. This is the aspect of Tefillin, whose mitzvah is opposite the heart — to subjugate desires and thoughts of the heart to His service. That is, to nullify all the fallen and broken loves through the light of Tefillin, which is the light of the holy Nekudah that dwells at Bris Shalom. Tefillin are called an "Os" [sign]: "Uk'shartam l'os al yadecha" (Devarim 6:8) — the aspect of Bris where the light of the Nekudah resides. This is the binding of Tefillin — literally binding: one binds the Tefillin (the light of the Nekudah) to the left arm, which is opposite the heart. The left is the aspect of Gevuros where the Sitra Achara has its hold — the disgraces and broken loves dwelling on the heart. Their shattering was due to the excess Gevuros within them. By binding them to the light of the Nekudah, they are rectified. Therefore the binding is with the right hand — where the light of holy love is rooted. Our Sages gave primary importance to the right hand because it ties Tefillin (Berachos 62a). The essential Tefillin are in the aspect of the right — Chesed, the light of holy love dwelling at the Bris. The Tefillin are produced through the Nekudah that rises in the light of day through engaging in Torah and prayer at night, as brought in the Kavanos. Our Sages said (Chagigah 12b): "Whoever engages in Torah at night, a thread of Chesed is drawn upon him by day" — this Chesed is itself the light of the Nekudah, through which Tefillin are made. This is the aspect of the Kesher of the hand — which is a Yud, the Nekudah in the aspect of Yud. This Yud emerges through the illumination of Yesod where the Nekudah's light resides, and it is closest to the heart. The essential illumination of Tefillin to the heart is only through this Nekudah — the Kesher of the Yud. In truth, the lights of Tefillin are exceedingly great, tremendous Mochin. But from them the light chains down and contracts from higher intellect to lower intellect through many levels, until the light of the Nekudah contracts into a Yud — the Kesher of the hand that illuminates the heart. This is the aspect of the blackness of Tefillin — the "black point." The essential rectification of the shattered is through the contraction of the light, for their shattering was due to excess light. The Tefillin, the Os/Yesod — the light that rectifies the shattered vessels — initially emerge from the forehead where the rectifying light emerges (as is known), through the aspect of se'aros [hairs] — contractions of light. Therefore they are black, for blackness is the contraction of light — black hairs — the aspect of the Nekudah, the lower intellect, the "black point" that illuminates through the brain's illumination. Then the Nekudah illuminates in the aspect of speech — "Pi yedaber Chochmos" — and illuminates the heart. This is the aspect of Tefillin. This is the aspect of Tefillin being from the hide of domesticated animal, wild animal, and bird. The fallen loves are the aspect of animalistic loves — for animals also have these desires. Therefore Tefillin are made specifically from them — elevating and sanctifying them with the holiness of Tefillin. The processing requires lishmah [for the sake of the mitzvah] — one must say with his mouth that it is for the holiness of Tefillin. Through this, the light of the holy Nekudah illuminates to the fallen loves (the animalistic aspect, the hide), and they return to holiness — from animal hide, Tefillin are made, which are holy. The essential sanctity comes through the writing, for the written letters are the aspect of the spoken letters through which the Nekudah's light is revealed — "Pi yedaber." Tefillin are in the aspect of uvda [action], and there one receives the Nekudah through action — through the written letters — just as one receives the Nekudah's light through the spoken letters of Torah, prayer, and yiras Shamayim. The writing on the parchment is itself the Nekudah illuminating to that which is below it — like the Nekudah of the Tzaddik/Rebbe illuminating to his student's heart. As stated in our Rebbe's words (Siman 192): the writing of ink on parchment — black fire upon white fire — is the aspect of Rav and Talmid: what is "blackness" (the lower level) relative to the Rav (the upper level) is "whiteness" (the beginning of Mochin) relative to the second level below it. The parshiyos in general are the aspect of Mochin, and they must be enclosed in the batim to receive their light through many contractions. From there one receives the light of the Nekudah in the aspect of Yud. This is the aspect of the hairs that protrude from the Tefillin — showing that the light of Tefillin only emerges through hairs (contractions). Just as the initial light of Tefillin from its source emerges through hairs, so too we can only receive its illumination through hairs — contraction of light — which is the essential rectification. This is also the aspect of wrapping the parshiyos in hair. This is the aspect of Tefillin shel Rosh and shel Yad — the three types of Tefillin: shel Rosh, the Kesher of the Dalet (also a type of Tefillin, as explained in the Kavanos of the Arizal), and shel Yad — corresponding to the three Nekudos: the comprehensive Nekudah of the Tzaddik HaDor; the Nekudah that all of Yisrael receive from each other (umkablin dein min dein); and the Nekudah each one receives minei ubei [from himself and his Creator]. Tefillin shel Rosh is the aspect of the Tzaddik — whose Nekudah is the "head" and "Mochin," from which all receive. He is called "Rosh Bnei Yisrael" — the aspect of Rebbe. The Kesher of the Dalet is the illumination that emerges from there — the Nekudah of Malchus, the totality of Yisrael who bind together and illuminate each other. This Nekudah illuminates through a "Kesher" (bond), for its essential illumination is through Yisrael binding together and illuminating each other. This is the aspect of the four camps of Yisrael. The essential element of the Dalet is the Yud — its kotz [point] — the Nekudah. The Dalet comprises a Yud and two Vavin — this second Nekudah illuminates in two directions, for each one must illuminate his own heart (Yud-Vav) and also illuminate his fellow's heart (another Vav). But the Nekudah of the Tzaddik HaDor (the aspect of shel Rosh) illuminates in the aspect of the Shin of Tefillin with three heads — corresponding to the three Nekudos, for the Tzaddik HaDor encompasses all three. Afterward comes the illumination of the third Nekudah that each one receives minei ubei — this is Tefillin shel Yad, from which the Nekudah illuminates as a Yud (the Kesher of the hand), illuminating to his heart. The totality of these three Nekudos is the Name Shin-Dalet-Yud (Shakai) — for this Name resides in Yesod where the Nekudah dwells. The illumination chains down from one to the next: the upper Nekudah (head) — the connecting Nekudah (middle) — the lower Nekudah (hand). In every level there are three: upper Chochmah and lower Chochmah — "Pi yedaber Chochmos" — two wisdoms. The Nekudah (Yud) comprises two Yuddin — upper and lower — and the drawing of illumination between them is the middle Nekudah (a Vav). This is: head, middle, end — the three Nekudos. The illumination from the upper to the lower Nekudah — from the Tzaddik HaDor to each individual — is accomplished through the totality of Yisrael binding together and illuminating each other. In truth, each individual is far from the Tzaddik HaDor and cannot receive from him except through the totality of Yisrael — through which the illumination is drawn, enabling each individual to receive too. This is the great advantage of many Jews being present with the Tzaddik — the essential reception from the Tzaddik who expounds "ba'rabim" (publicly), specifically — for through the multitude they have the power to receive his great illumination, enabling each individual to receive. This is the three types of Tefillin: shel Rosh and shel Yad — upper and lower Yud. Between them the illumination is drawn through the retzuos [straps] of the head, which draw the light from shel Rosh to shel Yad (as explained in the Kavanos). They contain the Kesher of the head — the binding and inclusion of Yisrael who illuminate each other, through which the illumination flows from the upper Nekudah to the lower. The essential Tefillin are only two (shel Rosh and shel Yad) — for the essential Nekudos are only two (upper and lower Yuddin). The middle Nekudah is only the drawing of light from one to the other, hence it has no parshiyos (Mochin). For receiving from one's fellow is only an illumination — even from one lower in level, one must receive from his Nekudah; and one can receive even without the fellow intending to illuminate — just from the Nekudah stirring from where it resides. But the essential reception of the Nekudah's light as Mochin is through the two main Nekudos: receiving from the Tzaddik HaDor (head/brain of the generation) and receiving minei ubei when one focuses his mind, stirs his brain, and speaks with arousal — then the Nekudah illuminates in him completely. This is the aspect of the Shin of three heads and Shin of four heads. The Nekudah is comprised of two Nekudos. Also, the comprehensive Nekudah of the Tzaddik HaDor (which encompasses all three) is itself comprised of two — for certainly this Nekudah too has a higher source above it. Even the comprehensive Nekudah of the Tzaddik is only the "lower Nekudah" relative to the Tzaddik — "Would that we could receive even from that!" But from the Tzaddik's own brain — the upper Nekudah — it is impossible to receive. Thus the Tzaddik has four Nekudos: his upper Nekudah, and his lower Nekudah comprising the three that illuminate to Yisrael. This is the Shin of four heads relative to the Tzaddik himself, and the Shin of three heads relative to Yisrael who receive the three Nekudos.

aligned_segments.he: כי רוב המאמרים של רבינו ז"ל שנאמרו ב~ אותן הזמנים כולם נאמרו על תפילין כך נשמע מפיו הקדוש בפירוש ואף על פי שכל מאמר כלול מכל התורה כולה אף על פי כן ביחוד היתה כוונתו בכמה וכמה מאמרים שנאמרו אז על מצות תפילין:
aligned_segments.en: Therefore Tefillin shel Rosh are revealed and Tefillin shel Yad are concealed beneath the clothing. For shel Rosh is the aspect of speaking with the Tzaddik whose words are all in the open — he expounds publicly. But shel Yad is the aspect of speaking between oneself and one's Creator — which is done in secret and modesty. The totality of the two Shins is seven heads — the aspect of Yesod, which is Shabbos, the seventh day. This is the aspect of Melupum [cholam] where the Nekudah resides — a Yud upon a Vav, the aspect of Zayin [7] — "Zachor es yom haShabbos." Therefore Shabbos is not a time for Tefillin (Menachos 36b), for Shabbos and Yom Tov are themselves an "Os" — the aspect of Bris where the Nekudah resides. On Shabbos and Yom Tov, the Nekudah illuminates by itself due to the inherent holiness of these days. This is the essential holiness of Shabbos — the holy Nekudah. Therefore on Shabbos all the worlds ascend to holiness, accomplished through the illumination of the Nekudah — all the shattered bind to the root of their Nekudah and are rectified. This is Oneg Shabbos — the fallen loves are nullified, and one merits holy delight: "Az tis'anag al Hashem" — "Then you shall delight in Hashem." Therefore Shabbos is not a time for Tefillin. This is the aspect of the three meals of Shabbos — corresponding to the three Nekudos. Therefore one must conduct Tefillin with holiness — it is forbidden to enter a bathroom with them (Shulchan Aruch 37:3), forbidden to treat them lightly, and one requires a clean body — not to pass gas while wearing them (ibid. 37:5). For Tefillin are the light of the holy Nekudah, which is the aspect of Shabbos, and Shabbos is "kevi'a v'kayma" — fixed and standing in its holiness always, never changing, never going out. Therefore one may not go out with them to unclean places — they are the light of the holy Nekudah itself, fixed in holiness forever, in the aspect of Shabbos — rest and fixedness — "Al yeitzei ish mimkomo bayom hashvi'i" — "Let no man leave his place on the seventh day" (Shemos 16:29). Therefore nighttime is not a time for Tefillin. The Nekudah dwelling at Bris, revealed as Tefillin, does not illuminate outward except through Malchus/speech — "Pi yedaber Chochmos." At night, Malchus dikdushah descends to the lower worlds to perform berurim [clarifications], hence the Nekudah's light cannot illuminate then. Only by day, when Malchus ascends with all the clarifications to holiness, does the Nekudah's light illuminate and Tefillin are made — for the Nekudah's light illuminates only through Malchus. This is the aspect of the three daily prayers — Shacharis, Minchah, Arvis — corresponding to the three Nekudos, for the Nekudos illuminate through prayer: "Pi yedaber." Shacharis and Arvis are the upper and lower Nekudos — day and night, shel Rosh and shel Yad. Minchah is the middle Nekudah — the Pesach [opening] that draws the illumination from upper to lower. Therefore Krias Shema is said only at Shacharis and Arvis — for the essential Nekudos are only the upper and lower (shel Rosh and shel Yad), which contain parshiyos/Mochin. Minchah is only the drawing of illumination — the aspect of the Kesher of Tefillin (middle Nekudah), which has no parshiyos — hence no Krias Shema at Minchah.

aligned_segments.he: ועיקר אור התפילין זוכין על ידי קימת חצות ועוסקין בתורה, ועל ידי זה חוט של חסד נמשך ביום (חגיגה יב) ועל ידי זה זוכין לתפילין כמובן בכוונות, קימת חצות זה בחינת העלאת היראה לשרשה על ידי בחינת משפט כי קודם חצות אומרים ווידוי על החטאים זה בחינת משפט ששופט את עצמו על כל מה שעשה, ואחר כך מתאבלין על חורבן בית המקדש שזהו בחינת תיקון המשפט כי חורבן בית המקדש הוא פגם המשפט כי מקום המשפט היה בבית המקדש וכשנחרב נאמר (קהלת ג) מקום המשפט שמה הרשע כמו שאמרו רז"ל (ויקרא רבא פרק ד'), כי בית המקדש היה כלול מכל הבחינות הנ"ל כי שם מקום היראה בחינת ירושלים יראה שלם (בראשית רבה פרק נ'), וגם הוא בחינת דעת כמו שאמרור ז"ל (ברכות לג) היינו העלאת היראה לדעת על ידי המשפט שהיה שם בבית המקדש בלשכת הגזית שהיו יושבין שם בית דין הגדול לעשות משפט למטה לבטל הדין של מעלה ושם מקום התורה כמו שכתוב (דברים יז) על פי התורה אשר יורוך:
aligned_segments.en: Minchah is the aspect of the Kesher — the aspect of Leah, the aspect of Dinim. Yitzchak established Minchah — the aspect of Dinim: "Vatichheina einav meir'os" — "His eyes dimmed" — the aspect of Leah: "V'einei Leah rakos" — "Leah's eyes were soft." The severity of judgment at Minchah is the aspect of Eisav's hold — "Vayishlach l'Eisav minchah." Leah contained something of the harsh judgment of Eisav — our Sages said (Bereishis Rabbah 70): Leah was destined for Eisav but through her weeping was saved from him. Therefore all the arrangements of prayer are at Shacharis — the upper Nekudah, which is the main one, containing all three. Avraham established Shacharis, and Avraham is the light of the holy Nekudah — Chesed: "Atah Kohen l'olam" (Tehillim 110:4). Therefore the main prayer arrangements are at Shacharis, when one prays with Tefillin at length — the essential Nekudah illuminates at Shacharis, the aspect of "Chesed l'Avraham" — the Nekudah being the light of Chesed. This is the aspect of prayer with a tzibbur [congregation]. The essential prayer is specifically with a tzibbur, for a tzibbur is not less than ten — and when there are ten, the light of the holy Nekudah (the aspect of Yud = 10) illuminates. Therefore one then says Kedushah, for there is no davar shebikdushah with fewer than ten (Megillah 23a) — for the Nekudah is called "Kodesh": "V'goy kadosh," and it is the aspect of Yud. This is the aspect of the three Kedushos: "Kadosh Kadosh Kadosh" — corresponding to the three Nekudos, each called "Kadosh." This is the aspect of the Shaliach Tzibbur's repetition. The Shaliach Tzibbur is the aspect of the Tzaddik HaDor, encompassing the entire congregation, the comprehensive Nekudah from which all Nekudos receive. As stated in our Rebbe's words (I, Siman 282): the Shaliach Tzibbur is comprised of all the good points of the entire congregation. Therefore, first everyone prays quietly, each one individually receiving minei ubei; through praying with a tzibbur they become included in each other and receive from each other; and then all together receive from the comprehensive Nekudah — the Shaliach Tzibbur's repetition. He repeats the prayer to illuminate to all the Nekudos. Then, during the repetition, they say Kedushah — three times "Kadosh" — the totality of all three Nekudos. This is the aspect of the severe prohibition of hotza'as zera l'vatalah [wasteful emission]. As explained above, the Nekudah dwelling at Bris Shalom is fixed in holiness always, never goes out, and only illuminates below through Malchus/speech. Therefore the holy drop that emerges from Yesod — the light of the holy Nekudah — is forbidden to be brought out except through the aspect of Malchus (one's wife). Then a tremendous rectification is accomplished — rectifying the shattered vessels, for all holy unions are for clarifying and rectifying the shattered vessels. Therefore the essential zivug is on Shabbos, when the Nekudah illuminates. But when, chas v'shalom, one brings the drop out in vain — he draws the Nekudah's light outward, as if destroying the world, giving them sustenance from the Nekudah itself, and renewing the shattering of vessels (as brought in the writings of the Arizal). Not only does he fail to rectify the shattered vessels through the holy Nekudah, but the opposite — he draws the Nekudah's light outward and the vessels shatter again. Therefore they said it is as if he uproots his mazal — for he uproots the Nekudah, the root of his vitality. And they said teshuvah does not avail him — for to where shall he return? He has damaged the Nekudah itself. As long as the Nekudah remains intact, teshuvah avails; but one who has damaged the Nekudah itself — to where shall he return? Yet in truth, nothing stands before teshuvah. As brought in all the sefarim, if he repents, he is certainly forgiven. But his essential teshuvah is only through the Tzaddik HaDor — the comprehensive Nekudah from which all Nekudos receive. Since he has damaged his own Nekudah, he must receive the Nekudah's light anew — which is possible only through the Tzaddik HaDor, the root of all the Nekudos. Similarly understood from our Rebbe's teaching "BaChatzotzerus" (Siman 5) on "Ozen shoma'as tochachas chayim" — the essential rectification of this matter is through the Tzaddik HaDor. Since by strict law teshuvah should not avail, yet nonetheless there is a remedy if he regrets and beseeches Hashem — this is purely gratuitous Chesed from Him, accepting in teshuvah one who is unworthy. And this is itself his rectification: by arousing Hashem's compassion, he evokes an entirely new Chesed that never existed before. The Chesed from of old cannot atone for him since teshuvah should not avail; but Hashem in His mercy now renews His Chesed to rectify and forgive even this sin. Since a new Chesed is necessarily drawn — through this he receives a new Nekudah (for the Nekudah is Chesed), and this is his rectification. The essential complete rectification of this is only through Mashiach, who will come speedily in our days. Mashiach will come primarily to rectify this sin, as brought in the sefarim — "U'nefutzos Yehudah yekabetz" — he will gather all the scattered from the four corners of the earth — the rectification of this matter. Mashiach is the aspect of the new Chesed that rectifies everything: "V'oseh Chesed limshicho" — "And does Chesed to His anointed" (Tehillim 18:51). "U'va l'Tziyon go'el ul'shavei fesha b'Yaakov" — "A redeemer shall come to Tziyon, and to those who return from transgression in Yaakov" (Yeshayahu 59:20) — "ul'shavei fesha" specifically — those who repent of the sin called "yildei fesha zera shaker" — "children of transgression, false seed" (Yeshayahu 57:4), as written in the Kavanos that this verse speaks of this rectification. To them specifically the righteous redeemer shall come — for their entire rectification is only through him. When he comes and rectifies them, the Nekudah comprising the three Nekudos will illuminate in them again. "Va'ani zos brisi osam… ruchi asher aleicha ud'varai asher samti b'ficha" — "This is My covenant with them… My spirit that is upon you and My words that I have placed in your mouth" — the Nekudah dwelling at Bris Shalom, where Ruach HaKodesh resides, as our Rebbe said; and it is revealed through the mouth — "lo yamushu mippicha umippi zar'acha umippi zera zar'acha" — "They shall not depart from your mouth, your children's mouth, and your grandchildren's mouth" — the three Nekudos: head, middle, end — three generations each receiving from the one above. All will illuminate and be revealed through Mashiach. "Amar Hashem mei'atah v'ad olam" — "Says Hashem, from now and forever" — for the final redemption is forever. Therefore we then say Kedushah d'Sidra — three Kedushos — the Nekudah comprising the three Nekudos. The matter of Tefillin according to the teaching beginning "V'atem tih'yu li mamleches Kohanim," which speaks of the elevation of Yirah (Siman 15), beginning: "Whoever wishes to taste the light of the Hidden Light (Or HaGanuz) must elevate the Yirah to its root in Da'as. How is it elevated? Through judgment — judging oneself." When one merits Da'as, one merits the revealed Torah (Torah Shebinigleh), the aspect of Sinai. Through the revealed Torah one merits Tefillah, "Chesed l'Avraham." Through prayer with mesiras nefesh, one merits the hidden Torah (Torah Shebenistar), the Or HaGanuz from the seven days of Creation. See there well. All this is the aspect of Tefillin. The essential purpose of Tefillin is to elevate the Yirah to its root. Tefillin are the aspect of Yirah, as our Sages said (Menachos 35b): "V'ra'u kol amei ha'aretz ki Sheim Hashem nikra aleicha v'yar'u mimeka" — "And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of Hashem is called upon you and they shall fear you — these are Tefillin." Tefillin are also the aspect of Mochin and Da'as — to elevate the Yirah to its root in Da'as. This is the aspect of Tefillin shel Yad (Yirah, "yad keihah") and shel Rosh (the root of Yirah in Da'as, head/Mochin). The Da'as is the aspect of Torah — the parshiyos of Tefillin. Krias Shema said with Tefillin is Torah, and through this one merits prayer — hence one prays with Tefillin. Through this one merits the Or HaGanuz — the surrounding lights (Oros HaMakifin) revealed through Tefillin, the hidden Torah, the Or HaGanuz. This is the Shin of three heads and Shin of four heads — the Or HaGanuz, the light of the seven days — the seven heads. For most of our Rebbe's teachings said in those times were all said regarding Tefillin — so we heard from his holy mouth explicitly. Although every teaching encompasses the entire Torah, nevertheless specifically the intention of many teachings said then was regarding the mitzvah of Tefillin. The essential light of Tefillin is merited through rising at Chatzos and engaging in Torah — through which a thread of Chesed is drawn by day (Chagigah 12b) — and through this one merits Tefillin, as understood from the Kavanos. Rising at Chatzos is the elevation of Yirah to its root through judgment: before Chatzos one says Vidui [confession] for sins — judging oneself for all one has done. Afterward one mourns the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash — the rectification of judgment. For the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash is the blemish of judgment — "Mekom hamishpat shamah haresha" — "The place of justice, there is wickedness" (Koheles 3:16), as our Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 4). The Beis HaMikdash encompassed all these aspects: there was the place of Yirah — "Yerushalayim — Yirah Shaleim" (Bereishis Rabbah 56) — and also the aspect of Da'as (Berachos 33a): the elevation of Yirah to Da'as through the judgment performed there in the Lishkas HaGazis, where the Beis Din HaGadol sat to render judgment below, nullifying the judgment above. There was the place of Torah: "Al pi haTorah asher yorucha" (Devarim 17:11). 1 Tikkun HaKlali — the General Rectification. Reb Noson equates it with rectification of the Bris and Da'as (knowledge/awareness), following Likutay Moharan I:29 and I:19. 2 The four Mochin: Chochmah, Binah, Chesed of Da'as, and Gevurah of Da'as. They correspond to the four parshiyos placed inside the Tefillin. 3 The Shin of three heads and Shin of four heads on the Tefillin shel Rosh: 3+4 = 7, corresponding to the seven orifices of the head (two eyes, two ears, two nostrils, mouth) and the seven clean days. 4 The three Nekudos: (1) the comprehensive Nekudah of the Tzaddik HaDor; (2) the Nekudah Yisrael receive from each other; (3) the Nekudah each individual receives from himself and his Creator (minei ubei). These correspond to Tefillin shel Rosh, the Kesher (Dalet), and Tefillin shel Yad respectively. 5 The Name Shakai (שד״י) — Shin-Dalet-Yud — is formed on the Tefillin: the Shin on the bayis, the Dalet in the knot of the head-strap, and the Yud in the knot of the hand-strap. 6 Leshon Targum — the Aramaic tongue. In Kabbalistic thought it corresponds to Kelipas Nogah, the intermediate shell containing both good and evil. Elevating its good into Leshon HaKodesh completes the Holy Tongue. See Likutay Moharan I:19. 7 The "entirely new Chesed" — when one has damaged the very Nekudah of holiness, the ordinary Chesed that enables teshuvah is insufficient. Hashem creates a brand-new Chesed never before revealed, and through this the person receives a new Nekudah — a concept deeply connected to the Rebbe's teaching on the ten types of song (Tikkun HaKlali). 8 Or HaGanuz — the Hidden Light created on the first day, stored away for the righteous in the future. It corresponds to the Torah's concealed dimension, accessed through Tefillin.
